description: Downloads a raw binary payload from a controlled HTTP server using WinHTTP, stages the downloaded bytes into local process memory, changes the memory region from writable to executable, and transfers execution directly to the downloaded payload through a function pointer call.

loader.role: downloads a raw payload over HTTP, allocates local memory, copies the payload into memory, changes memory protections, resolves WinAPI function pointers, builds a parameter structure, and calls the downloaded payload directly

payload.role: raw position-independent memory payload downloaded over HTTP and executed directly from memory

payload_source.role: NASM x64 source for the callable in-memory payload that writes the execution marker artifact

payload_behavior.description: The downloaded payload receives a PARAMS structure containing resolved API pointers, collects execution metadata, formats it into a buffer, writes a marker file, emits a debug string, and returns to the loader.
expected_actions: call GetCurrentProcessId through supplied function pointer
call GetLocalTime through supplied function pointer
call GetModuleFileNameA through supplied function pointer
format timestamp, PID, process path, and execution mode using wsprintfA
close marker file handle using CloseHandle

code_placement: Raw payload bytes are downloaded over HTTP and copied into private memory inside the current process without writing the payload itself to disk
execution_trigger: Direct function pointer call into the downloaded executable memory region
execution_target: current process local memory region containing downloaded raw payload

loader: WinHttpReadData loop used to retrieve raw payload bytes
payload bytes copied into allocated local memory
VirtualProtect changing memory protection to PAGE_EXECUTE_READ
GetModuleHandleA and GetProcAddress used to resolve API pointers for payload
parameter structure containing WinAPI function pointers
direct function pointer call into allocated memory
absence of CreateFileA or WriteFile usage for staging the downloaded payload to disk
absence of embedded shellcode byte array
absence of remote process injection APIs such as OpenProcess, VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, or CreateRemoteThread
payload: raw flat binary generated from NASM source
callable payload expecting PARAMS* in RCX
function pointer calls through PARAMS offsets

loader: sends HTTP GET request for raw payload binary
receives raw payload bytes over HTTP
allocates private PAGE_READWRITE memory in the current process
copies downloaded payload bytes into allocated memory
changes allocated memory protection to PAGE_EXECUTE_READ
passes PARAMS structure pointer to downloaded payload
transfers execution directly into downloaded memory buffer
payload: payload executes from private memory inside the loader process
payload retrieves current process image path
payload writes execution metadata to marker file
payload returns to loader after execution
process: no child payload process is created
no downloaded payload executable is written to disk
marker file is created by the loader process context
network: HTTP connection to controlled lab server
GET request for file_artifact.bin or configured raw payload resource
raw flat binary payload transferred over HTTP

semantic_meaning: Demonstrates a fileless network-to-memory loader pattern in which a raw payload is retrieved from a remote HTTP server, staged only in volatile process memory, provided with runtime-resolved API pointers, and executed directly without writing the downloaded payload to disk or spawning a second-stage process.

control_notes.payload_effect: creates a benign marker file confirming that the downloaded in-memory payload executed successfully

success_conditions: raw file_artifact.bin payload is downloaded successfully
payload bytes are staged into local process memory
VirtualProtect successfully changes memory protection to PAGE_EXECUTE_READ
required WinAPI function pointers are resolved
PARAMS structure is passed to the payload
execution transfers to the downloaded memory buffer
marker file contains timestamp, PID, process path, execution mode, and PayloadStagedToDisk: false
